It also settles title vs. hook: Jim’s title wins every field called “title”; the hook lives only in the hero and on the thumbnail.

Episode artwork now lives in the episode folder rather than generated_imgs/, as a PNG master plus an optimized 1080×1920 JPEG (~150 KB) for uploading to Squarespace. An episode is now a single self-contained directory.

sections.heading: Ep 145 audio — settling the source after a lisp & an echo
bullets: 6 June: Jim flagged that Trevor's voice sounded like a lisp after editing. Diagnosed it as Trevor's recording environment on a three-speaker session — exaggerated by processing, not introduced by it. Sent Jim three A/B versions to choose from: Riverside raw, Riverside with studio sound, and the Descript studio-sound pass.

8 June: Jim preferred the Riverside studio-sound version and asked to also strip filler words, pointing to the Riverside "magic episode" export. Posted a pass using the Riverside-cleaned audio with filler-word and word-gap removal (harsh cuts avoided), studio sound left off.

That pass came back with an echo. Traced it to source confusion on Riverside: Jim's magic episode export was 55 min, but the source pulled for editing was 58 min and carried the echo — the echo lived in the Riverside source, not in anything done in Descript. Re-pulled the correct source, re-cut all chapters, and shipped the 53:39 cut now live.
Open item: standardize which Riverside export we pull from so versions stop drifting — the 55-vs-58-minute mismatch is the root of this round-trip.

sections.heading: Audio player — loading deadlock fixed
bullets: The player could get stuck on the loading spinner until a manual page reload. Root cause: the .loading state disabled the play button (pointer-events: none), but Squarespace defers preload="metadata" until the user interacts — so the audio waited for a click that was itself blocked because the audio hadn't loaded. A true deadlock.

Play button now stays clickable while loading; the spinner clears on any readiness event (loadedmetadata, loadeddata, canplay, durationchange, playing) with a 2.5s hard safety net, and the chapter seek-markers wait for the real duration before positioning.

sections.heading: Embed gotcha — one non-ASCII char killed the whole script
bullets: A single em-dash (—) left in a JavaScript comment threw Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<' in the Squarespace-rendered page and silently killed all the player JavaScript — which masqueraded as an unrelated "audio won't load" bug.

Rule going forward: keep the entire <script> block pure ASCII, even in comments — Squarespace mangles multi-byte bytes in embedded scripts. Verify with a grep for code-points > 127 plus node --check on the extracted JS before handoff. Extends the existing three-contexts encoding rule.

sections.heading: HTML encoding — three-contexts rule established
bullets: Codified a rule for non-ASCII characters inside Squarespace code-block embeds: HTML entities in body (—, ·), \uXXXX in JS string literals ('\u2014'), \HHHH in CSS pseudo-content (content: '\2192').
Affects em dash, middle dot, right arrow, ×, −, ▾, é, smart quotes — never blanket-replace; the escape required depends on which context the character sits in.
